scope: Make production-reachable mobile conceal detection and retained NPC theft/decoy compatibility resolve players through the authenticated equipped-weapon PRE-CU combat level, and retire the post-Publish-14 Ranger blend/camouflage, Spy stealth/smoke, Smuggler ally-invisibility, urban/wilderness stealth, and Force Cloak families for players while preserving authored NPC levels, Publish 14.1 concealment, and retained later-content data and assets.

findings: Publish 14.1 Ranger conceal and Scout mask scent are skill-mod mechanics that remain production gameplay.
Pinned Core3 mobile camouflage detection compares the equipped-weapon PRE-CU player level with the detecting creature's authored level; it does not consume an NGE visible player combat level.
Pinned Core3 calculates that internal player value from private_<equipped weapon type>_combat_difficulty divided by 100 plus one and caps it at 25.
The authenticated project helper xp.getPrecuCombatLevel already implements the same player-versus-NPC boundary and is distinct from retained-content encounter difficulty.

Publish 14.1 has no player Spy theft or decoy profession actions, so those player entry points remain retired while retained NPC and expansion compatibility may continue to use their shared implementations.
Retained theft comparisons and decoy combat metadata must use the same PRE-CU player-versus-authored-NPC difficulty boundary instead of the removed NGE player-level field.

The authenticated Publish 14.1 skill table grants Scout mask scent, Ranger conceal, Jedi animalAttack at force_discipline_powers_mental_04, and none of the thirteen later action names in the retired invisibility family through native PRE-CU progression.

The legacy PRE-CU/NGE skill diff identifies later Ranger blend/camouflage, ranked Spy stealth/smoke, Smuggler ally-invisibility, urbanStealth, and wildernessStealth paths, while July 2005 post-CU notes document Force Cloak after the Publish 14.1 boundary.

The thirteen later action names, twelve matching buffs, command/combat rows, Jedi action, HEP, schematic, and visual compatibility surfaces remain loadable for NPC and expansion content, but cannot grant player gameplay authority; classic conceal and invis_cover remain outside the retirement set.
